messages:
ashley: FYI canary batch showed a subtle host-side perf regression for streaming chat. p50 CPU up ~8-12% on host-proxy when many small chunks arrive. :grimacing:

nate: ugh. did this start after the preparse refactor?

ashley: looks correlated. timeline -> preparse change + new minibatch hinting landed in canary 2h ago. infra-bot reported ramp: https://deploys.internal/redwood/canary/228 

rkumar: can you paste the flame or sample? quick check: is tokenize the hot path or writev/flush?

ashley: flame snippet (from perf.svg):

```
- host-proxy::handle_stream (40%)
  - preparse::parse_frame (18%)
    - tokenizer::tokenize_chunk (9%)
  - net::small_writev_flush (12%)
  - kvcache::lookup (6%)
  - scheduler::choose_kernel (3%)
```

ashley: main surprise is net small_writev still big. preparse move increased fragmentation, so more tiny frames hit the socket path.

maggie: so two vectors: tokenization CPU + increased syscall overhead from tiny writes. Can we batch writes at host-proxy side?

nate: we already have write coalescing but threshold lowered by the preparse patch. that was to reduce latency. tradeoff maybe wrong under load.

rkumar: hypothesis: preparse is producing more microframes which overflow minibatch window -> kernel selector sees higher variance and picks narrower kernels, hurting throughput. also increased kv cache thrash from more small contexts.

ashley: experiment idea: revert the minibatch-hinting adjustment and instead try: 1) increase write coalesce window by 2ms, 2) add a tokenization pool warmup for first 50ms of connection, 3) emit kernel-selection telemetry.

maggie: +1 for telemetry. we need a low-risk canary: only change coalesce window in canary-hosts and instrument. if no improvement, revert.

infra-bot: Canary cluster 22 has 32 hosts. current canary percentage: 5%. Deploy window: next 30m.

nate: I'll run microbench on host-proxy locally (script below) and share numbers:

```
./bench/stream-synth --qps 500 --chunk-dist small --concurrency 64 --duration 300
# baseline vs preparse-refactor
```

rkumar: I'll add kernel-selection tags: which kernel chosen, seq_len distribution, kvcache hit/miss per req, batch_size used. that should tell if misrouting is happening. will push a shim to canary.

ashley: thanks. initial raw numbers: baseline p50 latency 38ms -> canary p50 44ms; CPU host-proxy 6.2 -> 6.8 cores avg at same qps.

maggie: that delta is actionable. priorities: telemetry (rkumar), local microbench (nate), canary coalesce tweak (maggie). rollback plan ready if P50 > +15% or error rate increases.

nate: quick note: also saw more TLS handshake syscalls per connection in canary logs -> might be connection churn from client side chunking. adding keepalive metrics might help.

ashley: added one more: collect counts of small-write syscalls per request (write < 2k). looks like ~30% increase.

rkumar: if kvcache eviction increases we should also record hot-key fingerprint; maybe preparse split is moving prefixes that reduce KV reuse.

maggie: timeline: rkumar to drop telemetry patch in 10m, nate to run bench and paste numbers in thread in 40m, canary coalesce tweak in 60m if bench matches. I'll monitor canary dashboard. :eyes:

ashley: ping me on call if we need immediate rollback. I'll also attach sample pprof.
summary: host-proxy canary shows CPU + latency regression after preparse/minibatch hint changes; team agrees to add telemetry, run microbench, and try a write-coalesce tweak on canary.
